scientific_question: Does a higher reactive-astrocyte fraction within CA1 predict worse donor memory decline independent of standard neuropathology confounds?
approach: For each donor, load cell centroids and cell-type labels from the slide zarr, assign cells to annotation polygons by centroid-in-polygon after dividing CustomAnnotations polygon coordinates by 16, and restrict to the target region gate. Count cells labeled Astrocyte and Reactive Astrocyte, then compute the donor biomarker as n_reactive_astrocyte / (n_astrocyte + n_reactive_astrocyte). If the target region is absent or the denominator is zero, return NaN.

variations.name: candidate_variant_a
variations.description: CA1-only reactive astrocyte fraction among astrocyte-lineage cells: Reactive Astrocyte / (Astrocyte + Reactive Astrocyte) within CA1.

variations.name: candidate_variant_b
variations.description: Broader adjacent pyramidal-field gate: Reactive Astrocyte / (Astrocyte + Reactive Astrocyte) within CA1 plus CA2.

notes: Use all polygons for a named region and merge them implicitly through centroid assignment. Region assignment should use centroids, not contour overlap. Confirm the exact cell-label storage in ClassificationNode and map numeric codes to the Astrocyte and Reactive Astrocyte labels if needed. No embeddings or WSI pixels are required for this round.
rationale: With an empty panel, the strongest next test is a simple high-coverage, region-anchored cell-composition marker rather than a diffuse global summary. CA1 is a core memory-vulnerable hippocampal field, and reactive astrocyte enrichment is a biologically interpretable readout of local gliosis/injury that may retain signal beyond Braak and CERAD while being more robust than raw counts.
